title.zh: 卷329 列傳一百十六 宋元俊 薛琮 张芝元 董天弼 柴大纪
title.en: Volume 329 Biographies 116: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, Chai Daji
title.raw: 卷329 列傳一百十六 宋元俊 薛琮 张芝元 董天弼 柴大纪

sentences.zh: 列傳一百十六

translations.literal: Biographies 116
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 116

sentences.zh: 宋元俊薛琮張芝元董天弼柴大紀

translations.literal: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, Chai Daji
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, and Chai Daji

sentences.zh: 宋元俊，字甸芳，江南懷遠人。

translations.literal: Song Yuanjun, courtesy name Dianfang, was a native of Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanjun, styled Dianfang, came from Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 以武進士授四川成都營守備，遷懷遠營都司。

translations.literal: As a military jinshi he was appointed garrison commander of the Chengdu Garrison in Sichuan, and was later transferred to company commander of the Huaiyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military jinshi examination, he was appointed garrison commander of the Chengdu Garrison in Sichuan and later promoted to company commander of the Huaiyuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十年，孔撒、麻書兩土司構釁，金川、綽斯甲布兩土司乘隙為亂，元俊為撫定，集孔撒、麻書、金川、綽斯甲布、革布什咱、綽沃、白立、章谷、瞻對諸土司斷曲直，使頂經立誓。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of the Qianlong reign, the two chieftains of Kongsa and Mashu provoked conflict; the chieftains of Jinchuan and Zhuosijia took advantage of the opening to rebel. Yuanjun was sent to pacify them, gathering the chieftains of Kongsa, Mashu, Jinchuan, Zhuosijia, Gepusizhai, Zhuowo, Baili, Zhanggu, and Zhandui to judge right and wrong, making them swear oaths over Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 20 (1755), the Kongsa and Mashu chieftains feuded; the Jinchuan and Zhuosijia chieftains seized the chance to revolt. Yuanjun was dispatched to settle affairs, convening the chieftains of Kongsa, Mashu, Jinchuan, Zhuosijia, Gepusizhai, Zhuowo, Baili, Zhanggu, and Zhandui to adjudicate their disputes and bind them with oaths sworn over Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 累遷阜和營游擊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to brigade commander of the Fuhe Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to brigade commander of the Fuhe Garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，金川土司郎卡侵丹壩、綽斯甲布兩土司，諸土司請兵，署總督阿桂、提督岳鍾琪奏令元俊偕署副將長清諭各土司合兵進剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Jinchuan chieftain Langka invaded the two chieftains of Danba and Zhuosijia. The chieftains requested troops. Acting Governor-General Agui and Regional Commander Yue Zhongqi memorialized the throne ordering Yuanjun, together with Acting Vice General Chang Qing, to instruct the various chieftains to combine forces and advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 (1764), the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Danba and Zhuosijia chieftains. When the chieftains appealed for troops, Acting Governor-General Agui and Regional Commander Yue Zhongqi memorialized the throne directing Yuanjun, together with Acting Vice General Chang Qing, to rally the chieftains for a joint punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 移漳臘營參將，坐事左遷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regimental commander of the Zhangla Garrison, but was demoted for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regimental commander of the Zhangla Garrison, then demoted after being implicated in a disciplinary matter.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，小金川土司澤旺之子僧格桑掠鄂克什，阿桂檄元俊宣諭僧格桑還侵地及所掠番民。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, raided Ekezhi. Agui issued an order to Yuanjun to proclaim and instruct Senggesang to return the invaded territory and the tribal people he had seized.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 35 (1770), Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, plundered Ekezhi. Agui ordered Yuanjun to proclaim to Senggesang that he must restore the seized lands and return the tribal people he had taken.

sentences.zh: 复補阜和營游擊。

translations.literal: He was again appointed brigade commander of the Fuhe Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as brigade commander of the Fuhe Garrison.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木據革布什咱官寨，戕土司策楞多布丹，總督阿爾泰復令元俊往宣諭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the official stockade of Gepusizhai and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 (1771), the Gepusizhai headman Jielangkazi Suonuomu seized the chieftain's stockade at Gepusizhai and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor-General Altai once again sent Yuanjun to deliver an imperial proclamation.

sentences.zh: 小金川圍鄂克什、達木巴宗，侵明正土司，據納頂寨，元俊與參將薛琮、都司李天佑率兵討之，收納頂寨，進攻索布大寨。

translations.literal: Lesser Jinchuan besieged Ekezhi and Damubazong, invaded the Mingzheng chieftain, and occupied Nadingsai. Yuanjun, together with Regimental Commander Xue Cong and Company Commander Li Tianyou, led troops to attack them, recovered Nadingsai, and advanced to assault Suobudazhai.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Jinchuan forces besieged Ekezhi and Damubazong, encroached on Mingzheng territory, and seized Nadingsai. Yuanjun joined Regimental Commander Xue Cong and Company Commander Li Tianyou in a punitive expedition, retook Nadingsai, and pressed the attack on Suobudazhai.

sentences.zh: 琮率兵自山梁潛度，元俊與天佑渡河夾擊，獲石卡十八，屢戰皆捷，明正土司碉寨七百餘盡复。

translations.literal: Cong led troops in a secret crossing over the mountain ridge; Yuanjun and Tianyou crossed the river and attacked from both sides. They captured eighteen stone blockhouses and won repeated victories, fully recovering more than seven hundred watchtowers and stockades of the Mingzheng chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Cong led his men in a stealthy crossing over the ridge while Yuanjun and Tianyou forded the river to strike from both flanks. They took eighteen stone blockhouses in a string of victories and fully restored more than seven hundred watchtowers and stockades belonging to the Mingzheng chieftain.

sentences.zh: 師入小金川境，取噶中拉、莫如納、扎功拉等地，進克納咱。

translations.literal: The army entered Lesser Jinchuan territory, took Gachongla, Moruna, Zhagongla, and other places, and advanced to capture Nazha.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed into Lesser Jinchuan, seized Gachongla, Moruna, Zhagongla, and other positions, and went on to capture Nazha.

sentences.zh: 阿爾泰及侍郎桂林以聞，擢松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Altai and Vice Minister Guilin reported this to the throne, and Yuanjun was promoted to regional commander of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Altai and Vice Minister Guilin reported the victories to the throne, and Yuanjun was promoted to regional commander of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 師攻甲木，賊據喇嘛寺為固。

translations.literal: The army attacked Jiamu, and the rebels held firm at the Lama Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the army assaulted Jiamu, the rebels dug in at the Lama Temple.

sentences.zh: 元俊及守備陳定國攻破之，盡收所屬城、卡、碉、寨，據墨爾多山梁。

translations.literal: Yuanjun and Garrison Commander Chen Dingguo broke through it, fully recovered the affiliated towns, blockhouses, watchtowers, and stockades, and occupied the Moriduo ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun and Garrison Commander Chen Dingguo stormed the position, recaptured all affiliated towns, blockhouses, watchtowers, and stockades, and secured the Moriduo ridge.

sentences.zh: 師復進，天佑、定國攻西山梁，元俊同侍衛六十一、參將巴克坦布等自喇嘛寺繞攻郭松，參領普寧自西山麓沿河攻甲木，侍衛哈青阿及琮自東山麓攻卡丫。

translations.literal: The army advanced again. Tianyou and Dingguo attacked the western ridge. Yuanjun, together with Bodyguard Liushiyi, Regimental Commander Baketanbu, and others, circled from the Lama Temple to attack Guosong. Battalion Commander Puning attacked Jiamu along the river from the foot of the western hills. Bodyguard Ha Qing'a and Cong attacked Kayai from the foot of the eastern hills.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed forward again on multiple axes: Tianyou and Dingguo struck the western ridge; Yuanjun, Bodyguard Liushiyi, Regimental Commander Baketanbu, and others swung around from the Lama Temple to hit Guosong; Battalion Commander Puning moved up the river from the western foothills against Jiamu; and Bodyguard Ha Qing'a and Cong attacked Kayai from the eastern foothills.

sentences.zh: 師行以夜半，戰自卯至巳，卡丫、郭松、甲木皆克。

translations.literal: The army marched at midnight. Fighting lasted from the hour of mao to the hour of si, and Kayai, Guosong, and Jiamu were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The troops moved out at midnight and fought from dawn until mid-morning; Kayai, Guosong, and Jiamu all fell.

sentences.zh: 賜元俊孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Yuanjun was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor awarded Yuanjun a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，師攻革布​​什咱，元俊請於桂林，分兵為五道：一自郭宗濟野宗攻木巴拉博租；

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, as the army attacked Gepusizhai, Yuanjun requested of Guilin to divide the forces into five routes: one from Guozongjiyezong to attack Mubalabozu;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 (1772), during the campaign against Gepusizhai, Yuanjun proposed to Guilin a five-pronged plan: one column from Guozongjiyezong against Mubalabozu;

sentences.zh: 一自章谷渡河夾攻，俾賊前後受敵，兩軍既合，先據默資溝，截金川來路，進取吉地官寨；

translations.literal: one to cross the river from Zhanggu and attack from both sides, so that the rebels would be caught between enemies front and rear; once the two armies joined, they would first occupy Mozigou, cut off the route from Jinchuan, and advance to take the Jidi official stockade;
translations.idiomatic: one to cross the river at Zhanggu and pinch the enemy from both sides, then unite, seize Mozigou to sever Jinchuan's supply line, and advance on the Jidi chieftain's stockade;

sentences.zh: 一自巴旺之高石、嘉舉諸山，分道攻薩瑪多監藏布覺，取吉地；

translations.literal: one from the mountains of Gaoshi and Jiaju in Bawang, dividing into routes to attack Samaduojianzangbujue and take Jidi;
translations.idiomatic: one from the Gaoshi and Jiaju heights in Bawang, splitting to strike Samaduojianzangbujue and capture Jidi;

sentences.zh: 一自茂紐攻沙沖；

translations.literal: one from Maoniu to attack Shachong;
translations.idiomatic: one from Maoniu against Shachong;

sentences.zh: 一自喀勒塔爾攻黨哩，會兵取丹東。

translations.literal: one from Kaleta'er to attack Dangli, then combining forces to take Dandong.
translations.idiomatic: one from Kaleta'er against Dangli, then converging to take Dandong.

sentences.zh: 策定，元俊及游擊吳錦江等自章谷渡河據格藏橋，哈青阿、天佑出郭宗濟野宗，兩隊軍夾攻，賊驚潰，遂克木巴拉博租、薩瑪多監藏布覺諸地。

translations.literal: Once the plan was settled, Yuanjun and Brigade Commander Wu Jinjiang and others crossed the river from Zhanggu and occupied Gezang Bridge. Ha Qing'a and Tianyou marched out from Guozongjiyezong. The two columns attacked from both sides; the rebels panicked and fled, and Mubalabozu, Samaduojianzangbujue, and other places were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The plan adopted, Yuanjun and Brigade Commander Wu Jinjiang forded the river at Zhanggu and seized Gezang Bridge while Ha Qing'a and Tianyou advanced from Guozongjiyezong. The two columns caught the rebels in a pincer; the enemy broke and fled, and Mubalabozu, Samaduojianzangbujue, and neighboring positions were taken.

sentences.zh: 進克吉地官寨及默資溝。

translations.literal: They advanced and captured the Jidi official stockade and Mozigou.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to capture the Jidi chieftain's stockade and Mozigou.

sentences.zh: 參將常泰等克黨哩，都司李天貴等克沙沖，元俊复克丹東。

translations.literal: Regimental Commander Chang Tai and others captured Dangli; Company Commander Li Tiangui and others captured Shachong; Yuanjun again captured Dandong.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental Commander Chang Tai took Dangli, Company Commander Li Tiangui seized Shachong, and Yuanjun captured Dandong as well.

sentences.zh: 复革布什咱地三百餘裡，民戶二千餘。

translations.literal: More than three hundred li of Gepusizhai territory and more than two thousand households were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred li of Gepusizhai territory and over two thousand households were restored.

sentences.zh: 桂林遣陳定國調綽斯甲布兵駐軍界上，備調遣。

translations.literal: Guilin dispatched Chen Dingguo to mobilize Zhuosijia troops and station them on the border, ready for deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin sent Chen Dingguo to muster Zhuosijia troops and hold them on the frontier, ready for deployment.

sentences.zh: 上責桂林不令元俊乘勝取金川。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Guilin for not ordering Yuanjun to take advantage of the victory to seize Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor censured Guilin for failing to let Yuanjun press the victory and seize Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 元俊旋與散秩大臣阿爾泰劾桂林欺誑及諸罪狀，上為奪桂林職，令阿爾泰署四川總督，命額駙、尚書、公福隆安按治。

translations.literal: Yuanjun then joined Minister Without Portfolio Altai in impeaching Guilin for deception and various offenses. The emperor stripped Guilin of his office, ordered Altai to serve as acting Governor-General of Sichuan, and dispatched Imperial Son-in-Law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun then joined Minister Without Portfolio Altai in impeaching Guilin for deceit and other offenses. The emperor removed Guilin from office, appointed Altai acting Governor-General of Sichuan, and sent Imperial Son-in-Law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 未至，詔元俊督兵赴綽斯甲布率土兵進攻金川。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, an edict ordered Yuanjun to supervise troops and proceed to Zhuosijia to lead native soldiers in an attack on Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the investigators arrived, an edict ordered Yuanjun to take command at Zhuosijia and lead native troops in an assault on Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 元俊奏：「自戰失利，士氣消沮，現在兵力不足並按兩金川。

translations.literal: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since the defeat in battle, morale has collapsed. Present forces are insufficient to suppress both Jinchuans at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since our recent defeat, morale has collapsed. Our present strength is insufficient to subdue both Jinchuans simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 請敕調湖南、湖北、山西、甘肅兵二萬，分三道進軍，計兩月可竟事。」

translations.literal: I request an edict to mobilize twenty thousand troops from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu, advancing in three columns; I estimate the affair can be concluded within two months."
translations.idiomatic: I request orders to mobilize twenty thousand troops from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu for a three-column advance; the campaign should be finished within two months."

sentences.zh: 上以元俊請益師，未免張皇，令福隆安會阿爾泰、阿桂與元俊詳悉覈計。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yuanjun's request for additional troops unduly alarmist and ordered Fu Long'an to meet with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun for a thorough review and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Yuanjun's request for reinforcements as unduly alarmist and ordered Fu Long'an to confer with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun on a full reassessment.

sentences.zh: 上諭軍機大臣，謂：「元俊能治事，熟番情；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Grand Council, saying: "Yuanjun can manage affairs and understands tribal conditions;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Grand Council: "Yuanjun is capable and knows the frontier tribes well;

sentences.zh: 但其人似狡猾好事，當留意駕馭。」

translations.literal: but the man seems crafty and eager for trouble; care should be taken in controlling him."
translations.idiomatic: but he seems crafty and prone to stirring trouble—keep a firm hand on him."

sentences.zh: 尋，福隆安疏陳所劾桂林狀不實，上以方進兵，元俊熟番情，諸事不必窮究；

translations.literal: Soon afterward, Fu Long'an memorialized that the charges against Guilin were unfounded. Since troops were advancing, and Yuanjun understood tribal conditions, the emperor said there was no need to pursue every matter to the end;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fu Long'an reported that the charges against Guilin did not hold up. With the campaign underway and Yuanjun's expertise on the frontier indispensable, the emperor said not every accusation need be pursued to the end;

sentences.zh: 惟言：「桂林以白金畀金川贖被掠官兵罪最重，今汪承霈自承出其意。

translations.literal: but stated: "Guilin's gravest offense was giving silver to Jinchuan to ransom captured officers and soldiers. Now Wang Chengpei has admitted the idea came from him.
translations.idiomatic: but noted: "Guilin's gravest offense was paying Jinchuan silver to ransom captured officers and men. Wang Chengpei has now admitted the scheme was his.

sentences.zh: 承霈以曹司從軍，不當與其事。

translations.literal: Chengpei, as a provincial official accompanying the army, should not have been involved in this affair.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial official attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved.

sentences.zh: 當詰汪騰龍，成信讞。」

translations.literal: Wang Tenglong should be interrogated to establish a credible finding."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tenglong must be questioned so the truth can be established."

sentences.zh: 福隆安复疏言：「騰龍以金囑王萬邦待巴旺、布拉底克歸迷道官兵予金為賞，元俊誘萬邦令具札言桂林使贖被掠官兵。

translations.literal: Fu Long'an memorialized again: "Tenglong entrusted Wang Wanbang with silver to reward officers and soldiers from Bawang and Buladike who had strayed and returned. Yuanjun induced Wanbang to write a letter stating that Guilin had sent silver to ransom captured officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long'an reported further: "Tenglong had entrusted Wang Wanbang with silver to reward officers and men from Bawang and Buladike who had lost their way and returned. Yuanjun coerced Wanbang into writing a letter claiming Guilin had paid silver to ransom captured troops.

sentences.zh: 事為元俊陷。」

translations.literal: The affair was a frame-up by Yuanjun."
translations.idiomatic: The whole affair was a frame-up engineered by Yuanjun."

sentences.zh: 上乃怒，責元俊奸狡負恩，命奪職逮問，籍其家。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, rebuked Yuanjun for treachery and ingratitude, ordered his dismissal and arrest for interrogation, and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, denounced Yuanjun for treachery and ingratitude, stripped him of rank, ordered his arrest, and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 參贊阿桂疏言：「元俊在川日久，熟番情，為近邊土司所信服。

translations.literal: Campaign Adviser Agui memorialized: "Yuanjun has been in Sichuan for many years, understands tribal conditions, and is trusted by the frontier chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Adviser Agui memorialized: "Yuanjun has served in Sichuan for years, knows the tribes intimately, and enjoys the trust of the frontier chieftains.

sentences.zh: 諸將能馭番無出其右。

translations.literal: Among the generals, none surpasses him in managing the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: No other general matches him in handling tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣遇事多與詢商，冀收指臂之效。

translations.literal: Your servant consults with him on many matters, hoping to achieve the effect of moving finger and arm as one.
translations.idiomatic: I consult him on nearly every decision, hoping to make our efforts work as one coordinated force.

sentences.zh: 乞恩仍留軍中，倘奮勉出力，使詐使貪，原所不廢；

translations.literal: I beg grace to keep him in the army. If he exerts himself diligently, the use of stratagem or even greed need not be discarded;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be kept with the army. If he fights hard, his skill in deception—or even his appetite for gain—need not count against him;

sentences.zh: 如剛愎逞私，即據實嚴劾。」

translations.literal: but if he is obstinate and pursues private ends, I shall impeach him strictly according to the facts."
translations.idiomatic: but if he turns obstinate or self-serving, I shall impeach him without mercy."

sentences.zh: 上命留總兵，還所籍財產。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him retained as regional commander and his confiscated property restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yuanjun kept on as regional commander and his confiscated property returned.

sentences.zh: 元俊同副都統永平、博靈阿等潛赴墨壟溝，進至郡崢。

translations.literal: Yuanjun, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others, secretly proceeded to Molonggou and advanced to Junzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun joined Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others in a stealthy advance to Molonggou and on to Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 乘月督軍登山薄賊卡，正大霧，我師騰躍入卡，克山樑三道、碉卡二十有四，進克格魯克石。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of moonlight, he directed the army up the mountain to press against the rebel blockhouses. A heavy fog had set in; our troops leapt into the blockhouses, captured three mountain ridges and twenty-four watchtower blockhouses, and advanced to take Gelukeshi.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of moonlight he led the troops up the mountain against the rebel blockhouses. A thick fog hung over the field; our men vaulted into the positions, took three ridges and twenty-four watchtower blockhouses, and pressed on to capture Gelukeshi.

sentences.zh: 金川酋圖佔丹壩官寨，綽斯甲布土司發兵往助，阿桂奏令元俊增兵往剿，未行，卒於軍。

translations.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain plotted to seize the Danba official stockade. The Zhuosijia chieftain dispatched troops to assist. Agui memorialized ordering Yuanjun to add troops and proceed to suppress them, but before he could march, he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan chieftain tried to seize the Danba chieftain's stockade, the Zhuosijia chieftain sent troops to help. Agui memorialized ordering Yuanjun to reinforce and move against them, but before he could march, he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 元俊在邊久，善馭諸土司。

translations.literal: Yuanjun had been on the frontier for a long time and was skilled at managing the various chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun had spent years on the frontier and knew how to manage the chieftains.

sentences.zh: 往時賚諸土司繒帛輒窳敝，元俊必以善者，諸土司皆喜。

translations.literal: In former times the silk bestowed on the chieftains was often shoddy; Yuanjun always gave them good quality, and all the chieftains were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts of silk to the chieftains had often been shoddy; Yuanjun always saw that they received good cloth, and the chieftains were grateful.

sentences.zh: 元俊出行邊，諸土司率妻子出謁，畀以茶、菸、簪珥，視若家人。

translations.literal: When Yuanjun traveled the frontier, the chieftains would bring their wives and children out to pay respects. He would give them tea, tobacco, hairpins, and earrings, treating them like family.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjun toured the frontier, chieftains would bring their wives and children to greet him. He shared tea, tobacco, hairpins, and earrings with them and treated them like kin.

sentences.zh: 稍不循法度，即訶譴，皆悚息聽命。

translations.literal: If they strayed even slightly from proper conduct, he would rebuke them, and all would tremble and obey.
translations.idiomatic: Step out of line even slightly and he would rebuke you—everyone trembled and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 打箭爐徼外夾壩出沒，元俊至，無敢犯行李者。

translations.literal: Bandits lurked beyond the Dartsedo frontier passes, but when Yuanjun arrived, none dared touch his baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits prowled beyond the Dartsedo frontier, yet when Yuanjun passed through, no one dared lay a hand on his baggage.

sentences.zh: 諸番小有動靜，爭來告，以故元俊諸所措置皆中窾要。

translations.literal: Whenever the tribes showed the slightest movement, they vied to report it. For this reason, Yuanjun's every measure hit the vital point.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes reported even the smallest stir, which is why Yuanjun's every move hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 其得罪，上亦知其枉。

translations.literal: When he fell into disgrace, the emperor also knew he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell from favor, the emperor knew the punishment was unjust.

sentences.zh: 既卒，其子猶戍邊。

translations.literal: After he died, his son remained in frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, his son remained on frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，金川平。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41 (1776), Jinchuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 元俊部將張芝元請於阿桂，謂元俊有功無罪，徒以忤專閫被羅織，語甚切。

translations.literal: Yuanjun's subordinate general Zhang Zhiyuan appealed to Agui, saying Yuanjun had merit and no guilt, and had been framed only because he had offended the supreme commander. His words were very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun's subordinate Zhang Zhiyuan pleaded with Agui that Yuanjun had served with distinction and committed no crime, having been framed only for crossing the supreme commander. His appeal was passionate.

sentences.zh: 阿桂為疏請，赦其子還。

translations.literal: Agui memorialized on his behalf, and the emperor pardoned his son and allowed him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Agui memorialized on his behalf, and the emperor pardoned his son and allowed him to come home.

sentences.zh: 薛琮，陝西咸寧人。

translations.literal: Xue Cong was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cong came from Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父翼鳳，河南南陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His father Yifeng was regional commander of Nanyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yifeng served as regional commander of Nanyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 琮以廕生入巡捕營。

translations.literal: Cong entered the Patrol Battalion by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Cong entered service in the Patrol Battalion through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 累遷四川漳臘營參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regimental commander of the Zhangla Garrison in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Zhangla Garrison in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 阿爾泰討金川，以琮從。

translations.literal: When Altai campaigned against Jinchuan, Cong accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Altai campaigned against Jinchuan, Cong served under him.

sentences.zh: 克納頂、邊谷諸碉寨。

translations.literal: He captured the watchtowers and stockades of Nading, Biangu, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the watchtowers and stockades at Nading, Biangu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 溫福代阿爾泰視師，攻巴朗拉，琮戰最力。

translations.literal: Wenfu replaced Altai in supervising the army and attacked Balangla; Cong fought with the greatest vigor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenfu replaced Altai as commander and assaulted Balangla, Cong fought harder than anyone.

sentences.zh: 又克卡丫，取通甲木。

translations.literal: He again captured Kayai and opened the route to Jiamu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Kayai as well and opened the route to Jiamu.

sentences.zh: 攻阿仰東山，總督桂林與都統鐵保、提督汪騰龍將兵取墨壟溝，令琮將三千人自甲木、噶爾金後繞山道應大軍夾擊。

translations.literal: In the attack on A'yangdong Hill, Governor-General Guilin, together with Commander-in-Chief Tiebao and Regional Commander Wang Tenglong, led troops to take Molonggou and ordered Cong to lead three thousand men from behind Jiamu and Ga'erjin by a mountain route to coordinate with the main army in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on A'yangdong Hill, Governor-General Guilin, Commander-in-Chief Tiebao, and Regional Commander Wang Tenglong led the main force against Molonggou while ordering Cong to take three thousand men around the mountains behind Jiamu and Ga'erjin to coordinate a pincer.

sentences.zh: 桂林中道引還卡丫，又檄鐵保、騰龍令退。

translations.literal: Guilin turned back halfway to Kayai and also issued orders to Tiebao and Tenglong to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin turned back halfway to Kayai and ordered Tiebao and Tenglong to withdraw as well.

sentences.zh: 琮深入，糧盡，待桂林不至。

translations.literal: Cong had penetrated deep; his provisions were exhausted, and he waited in vain for Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had pushed deep into enemy territory, his supplies were gone, and Guilin never came.

sentences.zh: 桂林令都司廣著赴援。

translations.literal: Guilin ordered Company Commander Guang Zhu to go to his relief.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin finally ordered Company Commander Guang Zhu to march to his relief.

sentences.zh: 賊據高峰曰博六古通，險阻，廣著師不得度。

translations.literal: The rebels held a high peak called Bolugutong, which was steep and perilous; Guang Zhu's force could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the formidable peak of Bolugutong; Guang Zhu's column could not get through.

sentences.zh: 琮督兵直進，毀柵十餘，奪碉七十餘。

translations.literal: Cong directed his troops straight forward, destroying more than ten palisades and seizing more than seventy watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: Cong pressed straight ahead, tearing down more than ten palisades and seizing over seventy watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 賊力拒，琮督兵仰攻，中槍，沒於陣，軍盡覆，同死者都司張清士、陳定國等二十五人。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong directed his troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and died in battle. The entire force was destroyed. Among those who died with him were Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and twenty-five others.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought back hard. Cong led an uphill assault, took a musket ball, and fell in battle. His entire force was wiped out. Company Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo were among the twenty-five who died with him.

sentences.zh: 阿桂破翁古爾壟，立祠戰地祀琮等。

translations.literal: When Agui broke Wenguerlong, he erected a shrine on the battlefield to honor Cong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: After Agui broke Wenguerlong, he built a battlefield shrine to honor Cong and his fallen comrades.

sentences.zh: 琮在諸將中號能戰，元俊與最厚。

translations.literal: Among the generals, Cong was renowned for fighting ability, and Yuanjun was closest to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was counted among the army's best fighters, and Yuanjun was his closest comrade.

sentences.zh: 嘗與期旦日會師，孰後至當斬。

translations.literal: They once agreed to join forces the next morning, with whoever arrived late to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: They once agreed to rendezvous at dawn the next day, with whoever arrived late to be executed.

sentences.zh: 琮至後二刻，元俊遣騎持刀呼取薛參將頭。

translations.literal: Cong arrived two quarters of an hour late. Yuanjun sent a rider with a drawn blade calling for Regimental Commander Xue's head.
translations.idiomatic: Cong arrived half an hour late. Yuanjun sent a rider with a drawn blade shouting for Regimental Commander Xue's head.

sentences.zh: 琮望見笑曰：「琮頭當與賊，不與公也！」

translations.literal: Cong saw this and laughed, saying: "Cong's head belongs to the enemy, not to you!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong saw him coming and laughed: "My head belongs to the enemy, not to you!"

sentences.zh: 奮前奪數碉反。

translations.literal: He charged forward, seized several watchtowers, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He charged forward, took several watchtowers, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 元俊猶為琮請罪，以功論贖乃已。

translations.literal: Yuanjun still pleaded on Cong's behalf; only when merit was weighed against the offense was the matter dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun still interceded for Cong; only when his battlefield merit outweighed the offense was the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 及桂林誤琮戰沒，元俊憤激論劾，卒以是得罪。

translations.literal: When Guilin's error led to Cong's death in battle, Yuanjun, in furious indignation, impeached him, and in the end fell into disgrace for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Guilin's blunder cost Cong his life, Yuanjun impeached him in a fury—and in the end was himself ruined for it.

sentences.zh: 張芝元，四川清溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan was a native of Qingxi in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan came from Qingxi in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 以千總從副將軍明亮徵金川有功，積官至越巂營參將。

translations.literal: As a battalion commander he followed Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a battalion commander under Vice General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to regimental commander of the Yuexi Garrison.

sentences.zh: 金川酋以番僧诇軍事，芝元言於明亮曰：「軍事每為賊知，非去其諜，滅賊無日矣。」

translations.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain used tribal monks to spy on military affairs. Zhiyuan said to Mingliang: "Our operations are always known to the enemy. Unless we eliminate their spies, there will be no day of victory over the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchuan chieftain used tribal monks to spy on the army. Zhiyuan told Mingliang: "The enemy always knows our moves. Unless we cut off their intelligence, we will never defeat them."

sentences.zh: 會大風雪，明亮命芝元率數十人偽若以他事出者，宿番僧寺中。

translations.literal: A great wind and snowstorm came. Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to lead several dozen men, pretending to go out on other business, and lodge in the tribal monks' temple.
translations.idiomatic: During a blizzard, Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to take several dozen men, pretending to be out on other business, and lodge at the tribal monks' temple.

sentences.zh: 芝元故通番語，與僧飲甚歡，僧醉眠，芝元出寺聚柴焚之，僧皆死。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan already knew the tribal language. He drank merrily with the monks; when they fell drunk asleep, he went out of the temple, gathered firewood, and burned it. All the monks died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan already spoke the tribal tongue. He drank freely with the monks; when they passed out, he slipped outside, piled firewood against the temple, and set it ablaze. Every monk inside died.

sentences.zh: 賊諜斷，因招降其眾。

translations.literal: The rebels' intelligence network was severed, and he was thus able to induce their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy's spy network broken, he was able to induce many rebels to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋從成都將軍特成額駐兵江卡，捕夾壩，圍本肯賊寨，焚其碉，斃賊甚眾，擢懋功協副將。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Chengdu General Te Cheng'e in stationing troops at Jiangka, capturing bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many rebels. He was promoted to deputy vice general with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Chengdu General Te Cheng'e at Jiangka, hunting bandits, besieging the rebel stockade at Benken, burning its watchtowers, and killing many enemies. He was promoted to deputy vice general for distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 台灣林爽文為亂，芝元率屯練降番佐軍。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen in support of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 參贊海蘭察等分攻大埔林、中林、大埔尾三莊，芝元為策應。

translations.literal: Campaign Adviser Hailancha and others divided forces to attack the three villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei; Zhiyuan served as supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Adviser Hailancha and others split forces against the three villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei while Zhiyuan provided supporting action.

sentences.zh: 賊據小半天山，將軍福康安等自前山進，芝元與領隊大臣普爾普領兵別為一隊，夜半先發，繞大山夾攻賊後。

translations.literal: The rebels held Xiaobantian Hill. General Fukang'an and others advanced from the front hills. Zhiyuan and Lead Commissioner Pu'erpu led a separate column, setting out first at midnight and circling the great mountain to attack the rebels from the rear in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Xiaobantian Hill. General Fukang'an advanced from the front while Zhiyuan and Lead Commissioner Pu'erpu led a separate column that set out at midnight, swung around the mountain, and struck the enemy from the rear.

sentences.zh: 黎明，諸軍同抵山麓，攀援上，賊力拒，芝元先登，拔其柵，斬獲無算，並堵賊去路。

translations.literal: At dawn all the armies reached the foot of the hill together, climbed up, and the rebels resisted fiercely. Zhiyuan was first to ascend, pulled up their palisade, killed and captured beyond counting, and also blocked the rebels' escape route.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the columns converged at the foot of the hill and climbed under fire. Zhiyuan was first over the top, tore down the palisade, killed and captured without number, and sealed off the enemy's escape route.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爽文就擒。

translations.literal: Before long, Shuangwen was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Shuangwen was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，擢建昌鎮總兵，圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified, he was promoted to regional commander of Jianchang, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first twenty meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified, he was promoted to regional commander of Jianchang, his portrait was enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was numbered among the first twenty meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 尋調松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to regional commander of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀掠西藏濟嚨、聶拉木，上命芝元率屯練降番往討之。

translations.literal: Gurkhas raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet. The emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gurkhas raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet, the emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen against them.

sentences.zh: 芝元至，值大雪，山谷皆滿。

translations.literal: When Zhiyuan arrived, a heavy snowfall had filled the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan arrived in the midst of a blizzard that had buried the valleys in snow.

sentences.zh: 芝元手大刀指揮，士卒皆感激用命，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan wielded a broadsword in hand to direct operations; the soldiers, moved with gratitude, obeyed with all their strength, and the enemy fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan led from the front with a broadsword in hand; his men, stirred to gratitude, fought with all they had, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀再叛，芝元偕提督成德督兵攻聶拉木，守拍甲嶺隘口斷賊援，聶拉木遂下；

translations.literal: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan together with Regional Commander Chengde directed troops to attack Nyalam, held the pass at Paijialing to cut off enemy reinforcements, and Nyalam was taken;
translations.idiomatic: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan and Regional Commander Chengde assaulted Nyalam, held the pass at Paijialing to sever enemy reinforcements, and Nyalam fell;

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻濟嚨，复克之，賊懼，乞降。

translations.literal: pressing the victory to attack Jilong, recapturing it as well; the enemy grew fearful and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed the attack to Jilong and retook it as well. The enemy, terrified, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，論平定廓爾喀功，再圖形紫光閣，列後十五功臣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when the merit of pacifying the Gurkhas was assessed, his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the later fifteen meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58 (1793), when honors were awarded for pacifying the Gurkhas, his portrait was again enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor and he was numbered among the later fifteen meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 芝元少以小校事元俊，後乃雪元俊枉。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan had served Yuanjun as a junior officer in his youth, and later cleared Yuanjun's wrongful disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan had served Yuanjun as a young subordinate and later vindicated him after his wrongful disgrace.

sentences.zh: 人以是多芝元，亦益賢元俊能知人也。

translations.literal: People therefore admired Zhiyuan all the more, and also came to esteem Yuanjun's ability to recognize talent.
translations.idiomatic: People admired Zhiyuan all the more for this, and came to esteem Yuanjun's eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 董天弼，字霖蒼，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Dong Tianbi, courtesy name Lincang, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tianbi, styled Lincang, came from Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 自武進士授四川提標前營守備。

translations.literal: As a military jinshi he was appointed garrison commander of the Forward Battalion of the Sichuan Provincial Standard.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military jinshi examination, he was appointed garrison commander of the Forward Battalion of the Sichuan Provincial Standard.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，師徵金川，天弼在軍有功。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Tianbi served with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Tianbi distinguished himself in the field.

sentences.zh: 累遷維​​州協副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy vice general of the Weizhou Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to deputy vice general of the Weizhou Brigade.

sentences.zh: 金川酋郎卡攻丹壩土司，天弼偕游擊宋元俊諭郎卡歸所掠，毀所築碉，兵罷，遷松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Danba chieftain, Tianbi together with Brigade Commander Song Yuanjun instructed Langka to return what he had seized and destroy the watchtowers he had built. When the campaign ended, Tianbi was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Danba chieftain, Tianbi and Brigade Commander Song Yuanjun ordered Langka to restore what he had seized and demolish the watchtowers he had built. After the campaign, Tianbi was transferred to regional commander of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 旋擢四川提督。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Regional Commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 郭羅克部劫西藏入貢喇嘛，上命天弼按治，未得其渠，詔責其苟且。

translations.literal: The Golok tribes robbed Tibetan tribute-bearing lamas. The emperor ordered Tianbi to investigate and punish them, but he failed to capture the ringleaders, and an edict rebuked his perfunctory effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Golok tribesmen robbed Tibetan tribute-bearing lamas, the emperor ordered Tianbi to investigate and punish them. He failed to capture the ringleaders, and an edict censured his half-hearted effort.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，小金川土司澤旺子僧格桑為亂，攻鄂克什土司色達克拉，圍其寨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rebelled, attacked the Ekezhi chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 35 (1770), Senggesang, son of the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rebelled, attacked the Ekezhi chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his stockade.

sentences.zh: 天弼督兵駐達木巴宗，檄僧格桑斂兵退色達克拉，以其寨糧盡，乞徙達木巴宗。

translations.literal: Tianbi directed troops stationed at Damubazong and ordered Senggesang to withdraw from Sedakela. Because the stockade's provisions were exhausted, Sedakela begged to relocate to Damubazong.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi stationed troops at Damubazong and ordered Senggesang to withdraw from Sedakela. With the stockade's provisions exhausted, Sedakela pleaded to relocate to Damubazong.

sentences.zh: 天弼與總督阿爾泰議留兵戍焉。

translations.literal: Tianbi and Governor-General Altai agreed to leave troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi and Governor-General Altai agreed to leave a garrison there.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，僧格桑复圍達木巴宗，並略木耳宗、巴朗拉諸地。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and also seized Mu'erzong, Balangla, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 (1771), Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and overran Mu'erzong, Balangla, and other positions.

sentences.zh: 天弼自打箭爐出邊，徵省標及松潘、維州諸鎮協兵，行至眠龍岡，賊已得巴朗拉，築碉卡為久守計，且斷我兵路。

translations.literal: Tianbi marched out from the frontier at Dartsedo, mobilizing provincial standard troops and forces from the Songpan and Weizhou garrisons. When he reached Mianlonggang, the rebels had already taken Balangla, built watchtowers and blockhouses for a prolonged defense, and cut off our army's route.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi marched out from Dartsedo, mobilizing provincial standard troops and forces from Songpan and Weizhou. At Mianlonggang he found the rebels already holding Balangla, fortifying watchtowers and blockhouses for a long defense, and severing his line of advance.

sentences.zh: 天弼議襲山神溝以解達木巴宗圍，尋將四百人自山神溝至德爾密，克碉七，賊竄走；

translations.literal: Tianbi proposed a raid through Shanshengou to relieve the siege of Damubazong. He soon led four hundred men from Shanshengou to De'ermi, captured seven watchtowers, and the rebels fled;
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi proposed a raid through Shanshengou to break the siege of Damubazong. He soon led four hundred men through Shanshengou to De'ermi, took seven watchtowers, and the rebels fled;

sentences.zh: 再進取畢旺拉，賊乘霧來犯，土兵驚潰，德爾密、畢旺拉皆陷。

translations.literal: advancing again to take Biwangla. The rebels took advantage of fog to attack; the native soldiers panicked and fled, and both De'ermi and Biwangla fell.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced on Biwangla. The rebels struck through the fog; the native troops panicked and broke, and both De'ermi and Biwangla were lost.

sentences.zh: 天弼疏請罪，上以天弼所將兵本少，總督阿爾泰不預策應援，宥其罪，諭以「當奪勉。

translations.literal: Tianbi memorialized requesting punishment. The emperor considered that Tianbi's force had originally been small and that Governor-General Altai had failed to plan supporting relief, and pardoned his offense, instructing him: "You must strive to redeem yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi memorialized asking to be punished. The emperor noted that Tianbi's force had been small to begin with and that Governor-General Altai had failed to plan supporting relief, and pardoned him with the admonition: "You must strive to redeem yourself.

sentences.zh: 再不努力，獲罪滋重矣」。

translations.literal: If you fail to exert yourself again, your guilt will grow all the heavier."
translations.idiomatic: Fail again, and your guilt will only deepen."

sentences.zh: 天弼復將五百人自木坪陟堯磧，順山攻甲金達對面山梁，取碉二。

translations.literal: Tianbi again led five hundred men from Muping up Yaoji, and along the mountain attacked the ridge opposite Jajianda, capturing two watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi again led five hundred men from Muping up Yaoji and along the ridge opposite Jajianda, taking two watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 天弼以鄂克什牛廠當要道，分兵殲守廠賊，駐軍其地；

translations.literal: Tianbi considered the Ekezhi cattle station to lie on a vital route, divided his force to annihilate the rebels guarding the station, and stationed troops there;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Ekezhi cattle station lay on a vital route, Tianbi detached troops to wipe out the rebels holding it and stationed his force there;

sentences.zh: 乘勝上下截擊，木坪、鄂克什諸土司錯壤，要隘皆為我軍有。

translations.literal: pressing the victory to strike from above and below. The chieftains of Muping, Ekezhi, and neighboring territories interlocked in their domains, and all the strategic passes came into our army's possession.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed the advantage with strikes from above and below. With the Muping and Ekezhi chieftains' territories interlocking, every strategic pass fell to our forces.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊复襲據牛廠。

translations.literal: Before long, the rebels again raided and seized the cattle station.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels raided and retook the cattle station.

sentences.zh: 上以阿爾泰師久無功，奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Altai of his office because his army had long achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Altai of rank for his army's prolonged failure.

sentences.zh: 因責：「天弼始終貽誤，與阿爾泰同罪，奪官，留軍中充伍。

translations.literal: He also rebuked: "Tianbi has from first to last caused delay and error, and shares Altai's guilt. Strip him of office and keep him in the army as a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed: "Tianbi has bungled from start to finish and shares Altai's guilt. Strip him of rank and keep him in the ranks as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 如更退縮，正軍法。」

translations.literal: If he retreats again, apply military law."
translations.idiomatic: Retreat again, and military law will be applied."

sentences.zh: 尋命下成都獄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，天弼以甲金達山峻不可上，求間道，得溝在兩崖間。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi found Jajianda Hill too steep to ascend and sought a hidden route, discovering a ravine between two cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi found Jajianda Hill too steep to climb and searched for a hidden route, discovering a ravine between two cliffs.

sentences.zh: 會大風雪，天弼率兵自溝中潛度，遂至達木巴宗，擊僧格桑色達克拉；

translations.literal: A great wind and snowstorm came. Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang and Sedakela;
translations.idiomatic: During a blizzard, Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the ravine, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang and Sedakela;

sentences.zh: 潰圍出，並克木耳宗，迎溫福師與會。

translations.literal: breaking out of the encirclement, also captured Mu'erzong, and joined Wenfu's army.
translations.idiomatic: broke out of the encirclement, also captured Mu'erzong, and linked up with Wenfu's army.

sentences.zh: 上聞，命貸死，留軍中。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he ordered his death sentence commuted and kept him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, he commuted the death sentence and kept Tianbi with the army.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令天弼監火藥軍械。

translations.literal: Agui ordered Tianbi to supervise gunpowder and military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Agui put Tianbi in charge of gunpowder and ordnance.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，師克資哩，阿桂令天弼將五百人駐焉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army captured Zili, Agui ordered Tianbi to lead five hundred men to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 (1772), after the army captured Zili, Agui ordered Tianbi to garrison the place with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 尋予副將銜，授重慶鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted the rank of vice general and appointed regional commander of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted vice general's rank and appointed regional commander of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 命督兵赴曾頭溝，進至梭磨，梭磨土婦請以千人從。

translations.literal: He was ordered to direct troops to Zengtougou and advance to Suomo. The Suomo tribal chieftainess requested to follow with a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead troops to Zengtougou and on to Suomo, where the Suomo chieftainess offered a thousand warriors to follow him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When this was reported, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, the emperor awarded him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 天弼督兵攻堪卓溝，自間道出納云達，深入賊境五十餘裡，克山樑三，破碉卡三十餘、木城三。

translations.literal: Tianbi directed troops to attack Kanzhuogou, emerging by a hidden route at Nayunda, penetrating more than fifty li into enemy territory, capturing three mountain ridges, and breaking more than thirty watchtower blockhouses and three wooden forts.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi assaulted Kanzhuogou, emerging by a hidden route at Nayunda and penetrating more than fifty li into enemy territory. He took three ridges and destroyed over thirty watchtower blockhouses and three wooden forts.

sentences.zh: 迎溫福師會於布朗郭宗，克大板昭、木丫寨，得碉三十六、卡十六。

translations.literal: He joined Wenfu's army at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhai and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six watchtowers and sixteen blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: He linked up with Wenfu at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhai and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six watchtowers and sixteen blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 上以溫福已得布朗郭宗進克底木達，天弼所克不過空寨，疏語頗鋪張，手敕戒之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced to capture Dimuda, while what Tianbi had captured were only empty stockades; his memorial language was rather inflated, and the emperor personally wrote an edict admonishing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced to capture Dimuda, while Tianbi had seized only empty stockades; his memorial overstated the achievement, and the emperor personally admonished him.

sentences.zh: 尋授領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Lead Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Lead Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，復為四川提督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 (1773), he was again appointed Regional Commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時小金川已定，溫福督師進討大金川，令天弼以五百人守底木達。

translations.literal: Lesser Jinchuan had by then been pacified. Wenfu supervised the army in advancing against Greater Jinchuan and ordered Tianbi to hold Dimuda with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Jinchuan had by then been pacified. Wenfu led the advance against Greater Jinchuan and ordered Tianbi to hold Dimuda with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 溫福進駐木果木，號大營；

translations.literal: Wenfu advanced to station at Muguomu, which was called the Great Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu advanced to Muguomu, designated the Great Camp;

sentences.zh: 底木達當賊來路，為要隘。

translations.literal: Dimuda lay on the enemy's line of approach and was a strategic pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dimuda lay on the enemy's line of approach and was a vital pass.

sentences.zh: 溫福檄三百人益大營，又去其後援。

translations.literal: Wenfu requisitioned three hundred men to reinforce the Great Camp, thereby removing Tianbi's rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu requisitioned three hundred of Tianbi's men for the Great Camp, stripping him of his rear support.

sentences.zh: 時溫福以軍屢勝，不以賊為意。

translations.literal: At the time Wenfu, because the army had won repeated victories, paid the enemy little heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu, flush with repeated victories, paid the enemy little heed.

sentences.zh: 金川頭人七圖葛拉爾思甲布等以千餘人詐降，溫福使與廝養雜處，因誘諸降人為變，諗底木達兵弱無後援，六月乙丑朔，潛自山後擁眾攻底木達，天弼率所部二百人抽刀力戰，至夜半，賊以鳥槍數百環擊，殺之。

translations.literal: The Jinchuan headmen Qitu Gela'ersijia and others feigned surrender with more than a thousand men. Wenfu had them mixed among the servants and attendants, then incited the surrendered men to revolt. Learning that Dimuda was weakly garrisoned and without rear support, on the first day of the sixth month they secretly gathered a force from behind the hills to attack Dimuda. Tianbi led his two hundred men, drawing blades to fight with all their strength. By midnight the rebels surrounded them with several hundred muskets and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchuan headmen Qitu Gela'ersijia and others feigned surrender with over a thousand men. Wenfu quartered them among the servants, then incited the surrendered men to revolt. Learning that Dimuda was thinly held and unsupported, on the first day of the sixth month they secretly massed behind the hills and struck Dimuda. Tianbi led his two hundred men in a desperate blade fight. By midnight the rebels ringed them with hundreds of muskets and killed him.

sentences.zh: 越九日，劫大營，溫福亦死焉。

translations.literal: Nine days later they raided the Great Camp, and Wenfu also died.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days later they overran the Great Camp, and Wenfu was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 上先命天弼駐丹壩，旋命移駐布朗郭宗，軍中傳賊來犯。

translations.literal: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to garrison Danba, then ordered him to move to Bulangguozong. In camp it was rumored that the enemy was coming to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to garrison Danba, then to move to Bulangguozong. Rumors spread through camp that the enemy was coming.

sentences.zh: 時天弼方屯美諾，上命奪官逮治。

translations.literal: At the time Tianbi was encamped at Meinuo. The emperor ordered his dismissal and arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi was then encamped at Meinuo. The emperor ordered him stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 總督劉秉恬疏言：「天弼自美諾馳赴底木達，途遇賊，右脅中槍死。」

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Bingtian memorialized: "Tianbi galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, encountered the enemy on the way, was struck by a musket ball in the right side, and died."
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Bingtian reported: "Tianbi galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, met the enemy on the road, took a musket ball in the right side, and died."

sentences.zh: 仍以貽誤軍事籍其家，戍其子舉人聯伊犁。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, for having caused military delay and error, his household property was confiscated and his son, the juren Lian, was exiled to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, for military negligence his property was confiscated and his son, the juren Lian, was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 金川既平，獲七圖葛拉爾思甲布，傳送熱河行在，廷訊，具言天弼死事時力戰狀，乃赦聯還，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and sent to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe. At a court interrogation he fully described how Tianbi had fought fiercely at the time of his death. Lian was then pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitu Gela'ersijia was captured and brought to the emperor at Rehe. At court interrogation he testified fully to Tianbi's fierce fighting at the moment of death. Lian was pardoned and allowed to return, and was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 柴大紀，浙江江山人。

translations.literal: Chai Daji was a native of Jiangshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Daji came from Jiangshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自武進士授福建守備。

translations.literal: As a military jinshi he was appointed garrison commander in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military jinshi examination, he was appointed garrison commander in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 累擢至海壇鎮總兵，移台灣鎮。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of Haitan and then transferred to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to regional commander of Haitan and was then transferred to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年十一月，林爽文亂起。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign, the Lin Shuangwen rebellion broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qianlong 51 (1786), the Lin Shuangwen rebellion broke out.

sentences.zh: 爽文漳州人，徙彰化，所居村曰大里杙。

translations.literal: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou who had moved to Zhanghua; the village where he lived was called Daliyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen was from Zhangzhou and had moved to Zhanghua; he lived in the village of Daliyi.

sentences.zh: 時奸民相聚，號天地會，漳州人莊煙為之魁，爽文與相結，謀為變。

translations.literal: At the time wicked men gathered together under the name Heaven and Earth Society; Zhuang Yan of Zhangzhou was their leader, and Shuangwen joined with them to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men had gathered in a secret society called the Heaven and Earth Society, led by Zhuang Yan of Zhangzhou. Shuangwen joined them and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 台灣知府孫景燧馳詣彰化，督知縣俞峻、副將赫生額、游擊耿世文捕治，焚數小村以怵之。

translations.literal: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui hurried to Zhanghua and supervised District Magistrate Yu Jun, Vice General He Sheng'e, and Brigade Commander Geng Shiwen in arresting and punishing them, burning several small villages to intimidate them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui rushed to Zhanghua and directed District Magistrate Yu Jun, Vice General He Sheng'e, and Brigade Commander Geng Shiwen to arrest the rebels, burning several villages to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 爽文因民怨，夜糾其徒來襲，赫生額等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Shuangwen, exploiting popular resentment, gathered his followers by night to attack; He Sheng'e and the others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting popular resentment, Shuangwen rallied his followers by night and struck; He Sheng'e and the others all fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂破彰化，景燧亦殉焉。

translations.literal: The next day they broke Zhanghua, and Jingsui also died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they overran Zhanghua, and Jingsui died defending it.

sentences.zh: 傍攻諸羅、鳳山，皆陷。

translations.literal: They also attacked Zhuluo and Fengshan on the flanks, and both fell.
translations.idiomatic: They also struck Zhuluo and Fengshan on the flanks, and both cities fell.

sentences.zh: 大紀時以總兵守府城，賊分道來攻，大紀出駐鹽埕橋御之，擊沉賊舟數十，馘千餘。

translations.literal: Daji was then regional commander defending the prefectural city. The rebels came to attack by separate routes. Daji went out to station at Yancheng Bridge to resist them, sinking several dozen rebel boats and beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Daji was then regional commander defending the prefectural city. When the rebels attacked from several directions, he took position at Yancheng Bridge, sank dozens of rebel boats, and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 五十二年春，水師提督黃仕簡、陸路提督任承恩先後赴援。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-second year, Naval Regional Commander Huang Shijian and Army Regional Commander Ren Chengen successively came to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 52 (1787), Naval Regional Commander Huang Shijian and Army Regional Commander Ren Chengen arrived in succession to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 大紀出攻諸羅，克之，即移軍守諸羅。

translations.literal: Daji marched out to attack Zhuluo, captured it, and immediately moved his army to defend Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Daji marched out against Zhuluo, captured it, and immediately shifted his army to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 旋以守府城功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for his merit in defending the prefectural city, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his defense of the prefectural city, he was soon awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 上以仕簡、承恩師久無功，授總督常青將軍，渡台灣視師。

translations.literal: Because Shijian's and Chengen's armies had long achieved no success, the emperor appointed Governor-General Chang Qing general and sent him across to Taiwan to supervise the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With Shijian's and Chengen's forces stalled, the emperor appointed Governor-General Chang Qing as commanding general and sent him to Taiwan to take charge.

sentences.zh: 爽文攻諸羅，自二月至四月凡十至，大紀督游擊楊起麟、守備邱能成等出戰，殺賊數千。

translations.literal: Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo ten times from the second to the fourth month. Daji directed Brigade Commander Yang Qilin, Garrison Commander Qiu Nengcheng, and others to go out and fight, killing several thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen assaulted Zhuluo ten times between the second and fourth months. Daji led Brigade Commander Yang Qilin, Garrison Commander Qiu Nengcheng, and others in sorties that killed several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 爽文之徒張慎徽偽降，大紀察其詐，置諸法。

translations.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender; Daji detected the deception and punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender; Daji saw through the ruse and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 台灣諸府縣皆編竹為城，不耐攻，大紀以忠義率兵民誓堅守。

translations.literal: The prefectures and districts of Taiwan all had walls woven of bamboo that could not withstand assault. Daji led soldiers and civilians with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, swearing to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan's prefectures and districts all had bamboo-woven walls that could not withstand assault. Daji rallied soldiers and civilians with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, swearing to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 上嘉大紀勞，賜荷包、奶餅，下部議敘。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Daji's exertions, granted him a purse and milk cakes, and referred the matter to the ministries for commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Daji's exertions, sent him a purse and milk cakes, and referred his merits to the ministries for commendation.

sentences.zh: 六月，授福建陸路提督，仍兼領台灣總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Army Regional Commander of Fujian while still concurrently holding the post of regional commander of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Army Regional Commander of Fujian while retaining his post as regional commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 鹽水港者，諸羅通府城糧道也，賊來攻，大紀力御之。

translations.literal: Yanshui Harbor was the grain route connecting Zhuluo to the prefectural city. When the rebels came to attack, Daji resisted them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshui Harbor was the grain route linking Zhuluo to the prefectural city. When the rebels attacked it, Daji fought them off with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 上促常青赴援，予大紀壯健巴圖魯名號，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor urged Chang Qing to go to the relief, granted Daji the title of Brave and Strong Batur, and made him campaign adviser.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed Chang Qing to march to the relief, granted Daji the title of Brave and Strong Batur, and appointed him campaign adviser.

sentences.zh: 八月，上以常青衰老不能辦賊，命福康安為將軍，仍令大紀參贊；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because Chang Qing was aged and unable to deal with the rebels, the emperor appointed Fukang'an as general and still ordered Daji to serve as campaign adviser;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, finding Chang Qing too aged to suppress the rebels, the emperor appointed Fukang'an as general while keeping Daji as campaign adviser;

sentences.zh: 而常青令總兵魏大斌援諸羅，賊邀諸途，退駐鹿仔草；

translations.literal: but Chang Qing ordered Regional Commander Wei Dabin to reinforce Zhuluo; the rebels intercepted him at every turn, and he withdrew to station at Luzicao;
translations.idiomatic: meanwhile Chang Qing ordered Regional Commander Wei Dabin to reinforce Zhuluo; the rebels blocked him at every turn, and he fell back to Luzicao;

sentences.zh: 復令總兵蔡攀龍援諸羅，大紀出戰，迎入城共守。

translations.literal: Chang Qing again ordered Regional Commander Cai Panlong to reinforce Zhuluo. Daji went out to fight and welcomed him into the city to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing then ordered Regional Commander Cai Panlong to reinforce Zhuluo. Daji fought his way out and escorted him into the city to defend it together.

sentences.zh: 上移大紀水師提督，而以陸路提督授攀龍。

translations.literal: The emperor transferred Daji to Naval Regional Commander and gave the Army Regional Commander post to Panlong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Daji to Naval Regional Commander and gave the Army Regional Commander post to Panlong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，加大紀太子少保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Daji was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Daji was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上以諸羅被圍久，縣民困守，奮力向義，更縣名為嘉義。

translations.literal: Because Zhuluo had been besieged for a long time and the county people had endured the siege and exerted themselves in loyalty and righteousness, the emperor changed the county name to Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhuluo had endured a long siege and its people had fought with loyal resolve, the emperor renamed the county Jiayi, "Praise of Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 賊攻城益急，上密諭大紀：「不必堅執與城存亡，如遇事急，可率兵力戰，出城再圖進取。」

translations.literal: As the rebels pressed the siege ever harder, the emperor secretly instructed Daji: "You need not insist on perishing with the city. If matters grow urgent, you may lead your troops in fierce battle, leave the city, and plan a renewed advance."
translations.idiomatic: As the siege intensified, the emperor secretly told Daji: "You need not die with the city. If matters grow desperate, lead your troops in a fighting breakout and plan your next move from outside."

sentences.zh: 大紀疏言：「諸羅居台灣南北之中，縣城四周積土植竹，環以深壕，壕上為短垣，置砲，防衛堅固。

translations.literal: Daji memorialized: "Zhuluo lies at the center between north and south Taiwan. The county city is surrounded by piled earth and planted bamboo, encircled by a deep moat; atop the moat is a low wall with cannon emplaced—the defenses are solid.
translations.idiomatic: Daji replied: "Zhuluo lies at the heart of Taiwan between north and south. The county seat is ringed with earthen ramparts and bamboo palisades, a deep moat, and a low wall mounted with cannon—the defenses are formidable.

sentences.zh: 一旦棄之而去，為賊所得，慮賊勢益張，鹽水港運道亦不能守。

translations.literal: If we abandon it in a moment and it falls to the rebels, I fear the rebel power will grow all the stronger and the supply route through Yanshui Harbor also cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Abandon it now and the rebels will take it, their power will swell, and we will lose the supply route through Yanshui Harbor as well.

sentences.zh: 且城廂內外居民及各莊避難入城者共四萬餘人，助餉協守，以至於今。

translations.literal: Moreover, residents inside and outside the city walls and refugees from the various villages who entered the city total more than forty thousand. They have helped supply provisions and joined in the defense down to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, more than forty thousand residents and refugees from surrounding villages have helped supply the garrison and fought alongside us until now.

sentences.zh: 不忍將此數万生靈付逆賊毒手！

translations.literal: I cannot bear to deliver these tens of thousands of lives into the murderous hands of the rebel bandits!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot abandon these tens of thousands of lives to the rebels!

sentences.zh: 惟有竭力保守，以待援兵。」

translations.literal: I can only exert all my strength to hold and defend, awaiting relief troops."
translations.idiomatic: I can only hold on with all my strength and await relief."

sentences.zh: 上手詔謂：「所奏忠肝義，披覽為之墮淚！

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict saying: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears as I read it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Your memorial of loyal heart and righteous courage moved me to tears!

sentences.zh: 大紀被圍日久，心志益堅，勉勵兵民，忍飢固守，惟知以國事民生為重。

translations.literal: Daji has been besieged for a long time, yet his resolve grows ever firmer. He encourages soldiers and civilians, enduring hunger to hold firm, knowing only to place state affairs and the people's livelihood above all.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for so long, Daji's resolve has only hardened. He rallies soldiers and civilians, endures hunger, and holds firm—thinking only of the state and the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 古之名將，何以加之？」

translations.literal: What ancient famous general could surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: What general of old could surpass this?"

sentences.zh: 因封為一等義勇伯，世襲罔替，並命浙江巡撫琅玕予其家白金萬，促福康安赴援。

translations.literal: He therefore ennobled him as Baron of First Rank Yiyong, with perpetual hereditary succession, and also ordered Zhejiang Governor Langgan to grant his family ten thousand taels of silver and urged Fukang'an to hurry to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Daji as Baron of First Rank Yiyong with perpetual hereditary succession, ordered Zhejiang Governor Langgan to grant his family ten thousand taels of silver, and pressed Fukang'an to march to the relief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，福康安師至，嘉義圍解，大紀出迎，自以功高拜爵賞，又在圍城中，倥傯不具櫜鞬禮，福康安銜之，遂劾大紀詭詐，深染綠營習氣，不可倚任。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived, the siege of Jiayi was lifted, and Daji went out to welcome him. Daji considered himself high in merit, having received ennoblement and reward, and being still within the besieged city, he was too hurried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an resented this and impeached Daji for deceit, deeply tainted with Green Standard Army habits, and unfit to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, but—thinking himself high in merit after receiving a peerage and still recovering from the siege—he was too harried to perform the full ceremony of presenting arms and armor. Fukang'an took offense and impeached Daji for deceit, deep Green Standard Army corruption, and unreliability.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「大紀駐守嘉義，賊百計攻圍，督率兵民，力為捍衛。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Daji garrisoned Jiayi; the rebels attacked and besieged it by every stratagem; he directed soldiers and civilians and exerted himself in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Daji held Jiayi while the rebels assaulted it by every means; he led soldiers and civilians and fought to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 朕諭以力不能支，不妨全師而出。

translations.literal: I instructed that if his strength could not hold, he might preserve the whole force and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: I told him that if he could not hold, he might withdraw with his whole force intact.

sentences.zh: 大紀堅持定見，竭力固守，不忍以數萬生靈委之於賊。

translations.literal: Daji held firm to his settled view, exerted all his strength to hold and defend, and could not bear to abandon tens of thousands of lives to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Daji held firm, fought on with all his strength, and refused to abandon tens of thousands of lives to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 朕閱其疏，為之墮淚。

translations.literal: When I read his memorial, I was moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his memorial moved me to tears.

sentences.zh: 福康安乃不能以朕之心為心乎？

translations.literal: Can Fukang'an not take my heart as his heart?
translations.idiomatic: Can Fukang'an not share my view of the matter?

sentences.zh: 大紀嘗奏賊以車載槍砲攻城，今福康安言得賊攻城大車，又委棄槍砲，為我軍所得，足見大紀前奏不虛。

translations.literal: Daji once memorialized that the rebels used carts loaded with muskets and cannon to attack the city. Now Fukang'an reports capturing the rebels' siege carts and also abandoned muskets and cannon taken by our army—enough to show that Daji's earlier memorial was not false.
translations.idiomatic: Daji had reported that the rebels used gun-and-cannon carts against the walls. Fukang'an now reports capturing those siege carts plus abandoned muskets and cannon—proof that Daji's earlier account was true.

sentences.zh: 大紀又奏縣城食盡，地瓜、花生俱罄，以油K5充食。

translations.literal: Daji also memorialized that the county city's provisions were exhausted, sweet potatoes and peanuts were all gone, and they subsisted on oil dregs for food.
translations.idiomatic: Daji also reported that the city's provisions were gone, sweet potatoes and peanuts exhausted, and the garrison subsisted on oil dregs.

sentences.zh: 當時義民助餉，未必遽至於此。

translations.literal: At the time loyal civilians were helping supply provisions; matters may not have reached that point so quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal civilians were still supplying the garrison; things may not have been quite so desperate.

sentences.zh: 但大紀望援心急，以食油K5為詞。

translations.literal: But Daji, anxious for relief, used eating oil dregs as his plea.
translations.idiomatic: But Daji, desperate for relief, pleaded hardship by citing oil dregs for food.

sentences.zh: 普吉保、恆瑞兩軍尚復觀望不進，若云猶有餘粟，則兩路赴援更緩。

translations.literal: The armies of Pujibao and Hengrui were still watching and not advancing. If it were said that grain still remained, then the two relief columns would move even more slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Pujibao's and Hengrui's columns were still holding back. Had he said provisions remained, those two relief forces would have moved even more slowly.

sentences.zh: 此時縣城存亡未可知，安怪大紀過甚其詞耶？

translations.literal: At that time whether the county city would survive was still uncertain—how can Daji be blamed for overstating his case?
translations.idiomatic: The city's survival was still in doubt—how can Daji be blamed for overstating his plight?

sentences.zh: 大紀屢荷褒嘉，在福康安前禮節或有不謹，致為所憎，直揭其短。

translations.literal: Daji had repeatedly received praise and commendation; before Fukang'an his etiquette may have been insufficiently careful, causing resentment, and Fukang'an directly exposed his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Daji had been repeatedly honored; his manners before Fukang'an may have been insufficiently deferential, provoking resentment, and Fukang'an seized on his faults.

sentences.zh: 福康安當體朕心，略短取長，方得公忠體國之道。」

translations.literal: Fukang'an should enter into my feelings, overlook faults and take strengths, and thus attain the way of serving the public with loyalty and serving the state."
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an should share my view, overlook faults and value strengths—that is the way to serve the state with integrity."

sentences.zh: 侍郎德成自浙江奉使還，受福康安指，訐大紀。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Decheng returned from a mission in Zhejiang, acted on Fukang'an's direction, and denounced Daji.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Decheng returned from a mission in Zhejiang, acted at Fukang'an's direction, and denounced Daji.

sentences.zh: 上命福康安、李侍堯、徐嗣曾、琅玕按治，福康安臨致書軍機大臣，言：「大紀縱兵激民為變，其守嘉義，皆義民之力。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fukang'an, Li Shiyao, Xu Sizeng, and Langgan to investigate. Fukang'an privately wrote to the Grand Council ministers, saying: "Daji indulged his troops and incited the people to rebel; his defense of Jiayi was entirely the work of loyal civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fukang'an, Li Shiyao, Xu Sizeng, and Langgan to investigate. Fukang'an privately wrote the Grand Council: "Daji indulged his troops and provoked the people to revolt; loyal civilians, not he, held Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 大紀聞命，欲引兵以退，義民不令出城，乃罷。」

translations.literal: When Daji heard the order, he wished to lead his troops in withdrawal, but the loyal civilians would not let him leave the city, and he desisted."
translations.idiomatic: When Daji heard the order, he tried to withdraw his troops, but the loyal civilians would not let him leave the city, and he gave up the attempt."

sentences.zh: 事聞，上諭謂：「守諸羅一事，朕不忍以為大紀罪，至其他聲名狼藉、縱兵激變諸狀，自當按治。」

translations.literal: When this was reported, the emperor instructed: "In the matter of defending Zhuluo, I cannot bear to treat it as Daji's crime. As for his other disreputable conduct, indulgence of troops, and incitement to rebellion, these should naturally be investigated and punished."
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, the emperor said: "I will not count the defense of Zhuluo against Daji. But his other misconduct—bad reputation, indulging troops, provoking rebellion—must be investigated."

sentences.zh: 命奪大紀職，逮問。

translations.literal: He ordered Daji stripped of office and arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Daji stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 福康安尋以大紀縱弛貪黷、貽誤軍機，議斬，送京師。

translations.literal: Fukang'an soon recommended execution for Daji on charges of lax discipline, corruption, and causing military delay and error, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an soon recommended execution for lax discipline, corruption, and military negligence, and sent Daji to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上命軍機大臣覆讞，大紀訴冤苦，並言德成有意週內，迫嘉義民證其罪，下廷訊，大紀猶力辯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Grand Council ministers to review the finding. Daji pleaded his bitter wrong, also saying Decheng had deliberately shown favoritism and coerced Jiayi civilians to testify to his guilt. The case was sent for court interrogation, and Daji still argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Grand Council to review the case. Daji pleaded his innocence, alleging Decheng had shown favoritism and coerced Jiayi civilians into testifying against him. At court interrogation Daji still argued forcefully.

sentences.zh: 五十三年七月辛巳，命如福康安議棄市，其子發伊犁為奴。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of the fifty-third year, he was ordered executed in the marketplace according to Fukang'an's recommendation, and his son was sent to Yili as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of Qianlong 53 (1788), he was ordered executed in the marketplace as Fukang'an had recommended, and his son was sent to Yili as a slave.

sentences.zh: 論曰：元俊、天弼在邊久，熟情偽，習形勢，諸番仰其威惠。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yuanjun and Tianbi had long been on the frontier, knew truth from falsehood, were versed in terrain and conditions, and the tribes looked up to their authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Yuanjun and Tianbi had spent years on the frontier, knew the tribes' ways, mastered the terrain, and commanded their respect through authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 元俊戹於桂林，激而欲自白，不得直；

translations.literal: Yuanjun suffered adversity at the hands of Guilin, was provoked and wished to clear himself, but could not obtain justice;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun was wronged by Guilin, provoked into defending himself, yet could not obtain justice;

sentences.zh: 微阿桂右之，罪且不測。

translations.literal: had Agui not supported him, his guilt would have been beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: without Agui's support, his fate would have been beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 天弼又見嫉於溫福，驅至寡之兵以投方張之寇，既死猶尚以為罪。

translations.literal: Tianbi was again envied by Wenfu, driven with too few troops against a rising enemy, and even after death was still held guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi was envied by Wenfu, sent with too few men against a resurgent enemy, and even after death was still condemned.

sentences.zh: 若大紀有功無罪，為福康安所不容。

translations.literal: As for Daji, who had merit and no guilt, Fukang'an would not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Daji, who had merit and no crime, found no tolerance from Fukang'an.

sentences.zh: 高宗手詔，可謂曲折而詳盡矣，乃終不能貸其死。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's personal edict was tortuous and thorough in the extreme, yet in the end could not spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong's personal edict was painstaking and thorough, yet in the end could not save his life.

sentences.zh: 軍旅之際，捐肝腦，冒鋒刃，求尺寸之效，困於媢嫉，功不成而死於敵，若功成矣，而又死於法。

translations.literal: In military campaigns, men give liver and brain, brave blade's edge, and seek the slightest effect—yet trapped by jealousy, they die at the enemy's hands without achieving merit; or if merit is achieved, they still die by the law.
translations.idiomatic: In war men give their lives and brave the blade for the smallest gain—yet trapped by jealousy, they die at enemy hands without glory; or if glory is won, they still die by the law.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，可哀也已！

translations.literal: Alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how lamentable!
